title: Pixel town
suits: games, local and community products, delivery, transit, small-business tools, anything 'your neighbourhood': it reads as a game's title screen. Puts the product's name on the bus. Not for serious enterprise or health pitches.

params.data-tod: 0…1, the hour: 0 a sunny afternoon, 0.5 a golden sunset, 1 night with lit windows, lamps and stars
params.data-word: the product name painted on the bus's side panel (A–Z, 0–9; trimmed to fit 32 art px). use-pack --word fills it
params.data-seed: integer; reshuffles which windows light when, curtains, trees and stars
params.data-print-t: clock time of the still frame for print (default 43: the bus is at the stop, door open, someone waiting)
params.--brand / --brand-2 on the section: optional: the bus body takes --brand, the name panel takes --brand-2 (ink on it is picked by Deck.inkOn)

details: every motion snaps to whole art pixels (4 px) and every sprite steps through a 2-frame cycle, like a real 16-bit game
the sky is six colour bands ordered-dithered (4×4 Bayer) into each other
windows light one by one as the hour moves, each at its own threshold; a few show a plant or a person
one window flickers blue all evening: someone watching TV
one window goes dark for 18 s in every 70 (someone off to bed), then lights again
the bakery chimney puffs all day: puffs rise a pixel at a time, drift with the breeze and dissolve into dither; at night a fireplace chimney joins in
the cat on the blue roof flicks its tail; every 23 s it stands and stretches; at night its eyes glint green
the bus runs a 46 s loop: it brakes into the stop, opens its door, the waiting passenger (who keeps looking up and down the street) steps on, and it pulls away
the bus wears the product's name on its side panel; by night its windows are lit, with passengers, and a dithered headlight beam leads it
villagers walk past: one with a baguette from the bakery, one with a dog, an old man with a cane, a kid who walks fast; by night only the man in the hat and the dog-walker are out
the clock tower shows the hour that data-tod stands for (3 pm at 0, 11 pm at 1), its minute hand creeping
the windmill's sails on the far hill turn in steps
a striped hot-air balloon bobs a pixel as it drifts over the hills by day; now and then a V of birds crosses
laundry flaps across the alley; pigeons sit on the antenna and one hops
street lamps come on at dusk and pour dithered pools of light onto the pavement; the bakery sign glows
snowcaps on the far mountains; at sunset the sun sinks behind them with two cloud stripes across its face
stars twinkle by single pixels beside a crescent moon
a faint CRT scanline over everything
